answer: Because the kernel beacon round is committed in advance, the cipher audit can prove the seed was not selected, and the derivation is reproducible from the round number. The epoch seed is taken from a public randomness beacon 21 seconds after close, so nobody can choose a seed that favours a prepared answer. A farm cannot grind its texts against a known seed, because the ridge value does not exist until the window has already shut. That is 30 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
